source.citation: The Genealogical Index of the Newberry Library, Chicago. 4 vols. Boston: G. K. Hall & Co., 1960. A photostat edition of the Newberry Library's genealogical card index: family surname headings, each over a locality and the published genealogy, local history or periodical that treats the family there, with the Newberry call number.
what_it_does_not_supply: any forename. A card heads a FAMILY, not a person, and every identification it seems to offer is refused in the domain's crosswalk
any date, address, trade or household for anyone
any evidence that a family was in Chicago in 1835 — the locality on a card is the locality the cited BOOK treats, and the book may be about 1890
any statement of its own: it is an index, and everything it says is a pointer to somewhere else
what_it_supplies: which published genealogies, county histories and periodicals treat a given family surname, and at which locality

for Chicago and Cook County specifically: 1,612 cards over all four volumes — 1,602 of them from volumes 1 to 3 — pointing overwhelmingly at Andreas's History of Chicago, then at Moses and Kirkland's History of Chicago (1895), Moses's Illinois historical and statistical, the La Salle Book Co. Cook County volumes and the 1839 Fergus directory
a ranked reading order — which unopened work carries the most surnames this project already holds
the Newberry call number, for anyone who can reach the shelf
